releaseNotes: The twelve experience-card technique names are settled as a deliberate non-translation, closing the last open decision in ARCHITECTURE.md. The question was whether they get plain-language founder equivalents or stay internal labels behind one umbrella term, and the answer is neither half of that framing. Every other vocabulary in scripts/lib/founder-copy.ts is a machine enum whose only other reader is a validator, so inventing a human label costs nothing; these twelve are terms of art with literature behind them and are the live key set of the Retention Mechanics MCP, so an alias would be a second vocabulary for one concept — the twin-file failure this repo has been burned by before — and would take from the founder the ability to look the technique up, read its critics, and recognize it when a designer says it.

What a founder gets instead is one umbrella phrase for the deck as a whole, and the two HIGH-risk techniques keep their literal name where the founder attests to them. Softening the name of the thing being signed is the one move that would be actively wrong: "Variable Reward" carries a warning that any friendlier synonym launders away, and the founder is attesting to the mechanic rather than to a description of it.

check:founder-copy gains rule 4, because a decision to leave something alone rots faster than a decision to change it — nothing in the tree records that the absence was chosen. Three sub-rules: the umbrella phrase must survive in the emotional_design lane blurb, which is where a founder meets this part of the launch; attestedTechniques must equal the HIGH set the card stubs declare, so promoting or demoting a card cannot leave the founder-facing list behind; and no technique name may appear in bannedFounderVocabulary. The third is the one that matters most and is the least obvious — the banned table's contract is "say this instead", so an entry there would force exactly the euphemism these names must not acquire.

check:emotional-design now closes the risk-tier triangle. Tiers are declared in three places — the twelve card stubs, the experience-cards.md routing index, and ethics-guardrail.md §3 — and only the last two were ever checked against each other. That gap stopped being a docs disagreement the moment rule 4 started deriving the HIGH set from the stubs: an unchecked stub tier became a forgeable input to a consent surface. Four new codes cover stub-versus-index tier disagreement, an unparseable tier line, a stub nobody routes, and a routed card whose stub was deleted.

Name matching across the three files needed its own key. The index writes "Identity & Self-Expression", the stub heading writes "Identity and Self-Expression", and the stub filename writes "identity-and-self-expression"; the existing normalizeCardName keeps "and" as a word, so the ampersand and spelled-out forms of one card would not have matched and parity would have silently skipped exactly the cards with the longest names. techniqueKey folds all three forms together.

Ten fixtures pin the new rules, five per gate, and each was confirmed to fail before its rule existed rather than asserted to. The founder-copy fixtures build a fake skill root carrying the real dictionary and renderer plus a card-stub directory whose tiers they control — which is also why rule 4's dictionary reads come from the source file under --skill-root rather than from the module the gate imports: an imported constant cannot be varied by a fixture, so the rule would have been unfalsifiable. The four repeated per-phase reads of founder-copy.ts were hoisted to one while making that change.

One thing is recorded as still open and is deliberately not solved here. A signed ethics attestation is a point-in-time record, but nothing captures what the founder actually read at signature time — reword a blurb or a bright line afterward and the signed artifact silently claims something else was agreed to. That is a records-and-liability question rather than a naming one, so ARCHITECTURE.md carries it rather than a gate.

The product name stays b2c-mobile-business-launch. Founder call. The cost estimate for revisiting it stands — a one-time sync across ~/.codex, ~/.claude and ~/.agents plus skill-version.json — which is the reason not to spend anything on it now. ARCHITECTURE.md's "Open decisions" section is now "Settled decisions" and carries the reasoning for both, because an outcome recorded without its reasoning is an outcome that gets reopened.
